Space Engine - a free universe exploration simulator (link in comments)

Main page: http://en.spaceengine.org/

This is obviously related to the launch of No Man's Sky. I think most of the people content with that game seem to simply enjoy the endless exploration rather than any gameplay. On that front Space Engine is perfect. It's a labor of love being developed by a single user. There's no game per se, though it's gradually headed in that direction. It's just a simulation of our universe, able to be explored in impressive detail.

If you like, in the options you can disable all body procedural generation so the only stars present will be ones that are known to actually exist in our universe. And even the game is still massive. Really gives you a scale for the universe when at a speed where in a blink you go from the Earth to Mars, it feels as though you are sitting still when in deep space.

Another bright side is the simulator is being constantly developed, and of course will remain free. Like most things in technology, there are a lot of people doing things because they love to do them and not because they're trying to promise you the world just to make a buck off you.

Once a garden was established the surpluses could be dried, canned, or even sold outside of the prison. Chickens would be allowed for eggs, fertilizer, and meat. Depending on the prison small domesticated animals like turkey, goats, or rabbits, could also be allowed. Given a sufficient amount of land, it would be be impressive what some felons could accomplish with this freedom.

All work on the farm/garden would be done by the prisoners but owned by the prison. The prison would be an incorporated entity comprised of the inmates, guards, with the warden as acting CEO. In my prison system the prisoners could convince the warden to buy sewing machines, thread, and fabric. The inmates could then make clothes and sale them on the market for a profit. These prisoners would be allowed to make their own clothing as well. The entire point of the system would be to encourage an entrepreneurial spirit.

In this fantasy prison, artists would be allowed to create and even sale their art on the internet. Prisoners would be encouraged to legally make money while within the confines of the prison. A system of welfare or allowance ($1/day) would need to be given to all inmates so they could pay for their own food (from the food stocks grown in the prison). A strict emphasis on discipline would be necessary. Loud speakers would interrupt a prisoner the very moment they broke a rule.There would be an absolute zero tolerance policy for all forms of violence. The entire premises would be monitored by guards and recorded at all times. The only privacy given to the inmates would be behind the curtain of their bed/toilet, or between two rows of corn. Supervised computer/media/internet/phone use would be allowed on a limited but frequent basis (1 hour/day or 7 hours/week). This would be of no charge to the inmates.
